If it is obvious that renewable and temperature instrument has a contemporaneous effect on electricity price,
it is not as such for gas.
There could be a lag between gas price and electricity price.
I have 1M futures contract for gas.
I can find spot price as well.
To be compared with electricity price

```{r}
ggplot(data= IV_data)+
  geom_line(aes(x=Date, y=spot_price, color="electricity"))+
  geom_line(aes(x=Date, y=gas_price, color="gas"))+
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
ggplot(data= IV_data)+
  geom_line(aes(x=Date, y=log(spot_price) - log(lag(spot_price)), color="electricity"))+
  geom_line(aes(x=Date, y=log(gas_price) - log(lag(gas_price)), color="gas"))+
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}

gas_elec_data <- IV_data %>% 
  mutate(log_diff_gas = log(gas_price) - log(lag(gas_price)))

gas_elec_data[is.na(gas_elec_data)] <- 0


cor(gas_elec_data$log_diff_gas, gas_elec_data$log_diff)
cor(gas_elec_data$spot_price, gas_elec_data$gas_price)

```
```{r}
gas_elec_data[, c("log_diff", "log_diff_gas", "Date")]
```

Une remarque gas supply shocks should be a good instrument for gas growth not necessarily for gas price.
But renewables should be good instrument for price levels.

```{r}
model <- lm(data = gas_elec_data, log_diff ~ log_diff_gas)
summary(model)
```
